sprints.goal: Data Foundation — all 6 master tables (Supplier, Staff, Dealer, Grade, Trading Size-Design, Design-Grade map), CRUD admin screens, soft-delete, seed data per sample PRD, PostgreSQL schema, Alembic baseline migration.
sprints.scope_notes: Establishes the relational backbone before any transactional work. Includes the FastAPI + Next.js skeleton, Docker compose for Postgres, and the admin CRUD pages that prove the full stack works end-to-end. No transaction forms, no stock ledger logic yet.

sprints.goal: Transaction Forms + Stock Ledger — Inward, Sales, and Adjustment forms with grade-row auto-population, atomic header+lines+ledger writes, row-level locking on (design_id, grade_id), and basic ledger read API.
sprints.scope_notes: Delivers all 3 transactional forms end-to-end. Stock ledger writes happen inside the same DB transaction as the form save (DS-002). Includes the GET /designs/{id}/grades-with-cb endpoint that Adjustment needs. F-012 (carry-forward) is implicitly enforced by the ledger logic but is explicitly tested in S3.

sprints.goal: Reporting & Carry-Forward — Stock Dashboard (date-filtered), Sales Report (Consolidation + Transaction dual-pane with multi-select filters), explicit verification of monthly carry-forward including back-dated transactions across month boundaries.
sprints.scope_notes: Read-side completion of the system. Dashboard reads from materialised stock_ledger (DS-003); Sales Report executes the dual-payload query in M-005. Carry-forward is exercised via integration tests using back-dated transactions per AC-053.
